findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok) and their "Best hostels >" lines, at both widths
findings.fault: The cards don't do anything. Each looks clickable: a white raised card, a link-coloured "Best hostels" line with a chevron, and a hover rule. But the parts map lists the card and its "Best hostels" line as static, so a click does nothing. Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of the page's three jobs, and this is the only place it can happen. "Explore destinations" in the hero and "Destinations" in the nav both jump down to these dead cards.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning a Bali or Lombok trip who taps "Canggu · Best hostels" to see hostels, gets nothing, and finds no other way to reach a guide. The tap fails silently, so they may think the site is broken.

findings.where: Nav bar "How we rank" link, and the same link in the footer
findings.fault: The link points back to this page, so it opens nothing. A visitor who clicks it to read how hostels are ranked stays where they are. The project says its ranking methods are published, so a dead link here leaves that promise without its proof.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who is wary of booking sites and wants to check the "merit alone" claim before giving an email. Clicking does nothing, and the claim now looks hollow.

findings.fault: All three are underlined like links and point back to this page, so none of them opens anything. The page asks for the visitor's email, but its privacy link leads nowhere, and there is no working way to report content.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to send their email address checks the privacy policy first and finds none. A hostel owner who wants to report wrong content about their property hits a dead link.

findings.where: Hero primary action: coral button "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news"
findings.fault: There is no sign-up form. The main action is a mailto link: it opens the visitor's mail app and leaves them to write their own email, with no subject, no guidance and no confirmation that they are on a list. On a phone with no mail app set up, or for someone who uses webmail, the tap opens nothing useful or a setup screen. The button label is also a full email address, which tells people how it works, not what they get.
findings.who_objects: A traveller on a phone in transit who wants launch news: one tap should sign them up. Instead they land in a mail app, unsure what to write, and many will give up. The founder loses those contacts.

findings.where: Nav bar on desktop: "Destinations" against "How we rank"
findings.fault: The two nav links look different: "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not, though both are links of the same kind. One plain item next to one underlined item reads like a current-page marker or a difference in function. The rules file reserves a different cue for the current page (semibold, no underline), and neither link is the current page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the nav who reads "Destinations" as not a link, or "How we rank" as the page they're already on, and so doesn't try one of them.
